title: Room to Spare for Entertainment
text: “So even Sadeena-san can’t stop them, huh…”

“Raphtalia-chan in particular has been trying really hard, but you know—when I tell her that in the current state of Melromarc, folks actually want the abuse angle more, so maybe she should quit pushing back against it, she just won’t budge.”
“Hmm… well, I can’t deny there’s a certain demand for Theo and Shion’s abuse show.”

Father agreed with a sour look on his face. Indeed, it was true that some customers had taken quite a liking to that particular show from the very beginning. When Father found it too much to bear, Lazy Pig would step in as his stand-in. Lately, the mixed-breed lizardman and rabbit-man have gotten used to it too.
“But that doesn’t mean I’m about to switch Raphtalia-chan and the others over to that side, even if some customers are getting bored of the current act.”
“Of course not. Naofumi-chan, you’re worn out every single day as it is—Theo-chan and Shion-chan cheer more energetically than you do, honestly.”
Older Sister gave a little chuckle at that.

“Well… so, thinking of something more substantial that Raphtalia-chan and the others could actually take part in as practice—maybe something like backup dancers behind the Filolials’ chorus line, juggling in the back, or riding on their backs waving both hands, that sort of thing?”
“Keel-chan said she wanted to try tightrope walking or a trapeze act.”

“Keel-kun sure is full of energy… According to the slave trader’s underlings, she’s the type who gets scolded for messing up during training. It goes—like—the human crosses it perfectly and the demi-human fails, that’s the script.”
Father declared it deplorable.
“In any case, well…” Father rested his elbows on the table, sounding somewhat like he was about to complain.
“It’s not as profitable as I expected… Right now it basically amounts to being the slave trader’s lapdog—hauling and brokering slaves for nobles, that’s the main gig.”

Indeed. Nominally, the circus was putting on all sorts of acts, but the growth in revenue wasn’t exactly glowing, I say. Of course, there were townsfolk and villagers who gathered cheerfully around the tent, enjoying the atmosphere, but circus tickets were only being bought by the small fraction of people who actually had money to spare. According to Father and Lazy Pig, the Three Heroes Church and bandit-hunting were turning out to be more lucrative than this.
“Oh my, that does sound rough.”
“Well, it’s still early days, I suppose, but I do know the other reasons… what to do about it, though.”
When Father used to go peddling, he did quite brisk business, to the point where he was even called the Holy Sage of the Sacred Bird. So what was different this time?
“What might the reason be, I wonder?”

“Ah… well, to put it plainly, neither the towns nor the villages have any room to spare. The Waves have caused famine, apparently. The crops have taken a real beating, and the seas are too rough for fishing to go well either. So people just can’t afford to spend on entertainment. There’s a lot of folks selling themselves into servitude too.”

Hmm… indeed, to enjoy entertainment like a circus, one needs some slack in daily life. With the Waves stirring up monsters and danger on top of it all, and sickness spreading besides—there was demand for medicine, sure, but a circus fell outside the realm of necessity.

“Elena-san went so far as to say I’d make more money running a food stall in front of the circus than the circus itself. Apparently it’s more profitable to butcher monsters we run into along the road, sell the meat cheap, and let people watch the circus on the side.”
“Oh my, Naofumi-chan’s cooking really is delicious, isn’t it—Sadeena wouldn’t mind you whipping up something to go with her drinks, either.”
“It’s not a food cart. Well… setting up a stall in front of the circus does sound like a decent idea. Either way, stability is what matters most.”

Hmm… it seemed my request to Father—to avoid peddling this time around, since I wanted to try something different from the usual loop—had backfired somewhat. Still, we needed to secure funds to search for and purchase Big Sister’s friends, without it looking unnatural. That, after all, was the whole point of touring Melromarc with this circus in the first place.

“What with maintenance costs, wages for staff besides the slaves, advertising fees—Elena-san’s been on my case about all of it… I feel like we need some kind of dramatic hook to really loosen the citizens’ purse strings at the root… otherwise we’ll just end up stuck as a circus that only draws crowds for the abuse show.”

Father grumbled that at this rate, everyone digging in the mines together would probably turn a better profit. The food shortage was a problem that absolutely had to be solved. It was rather frustrating that there was no way around it, I say. But if it was necessary to loosen the grip on the populace’s purse strings, then I, Motoyasu, would gladly lift restriction after restriction. Not that it needed to be broadcast as either Father’s or my own personal achievement.
“Understood. I’m somewhat reluctant, but I too shall bare an arm for this cause, I say.”
“You’ve got a solution in mind?”
“Naturally. I shall report the details to Father shortly.”
Naturally, this meant I would secure the Bioplant and spread it around.
“I shall secure a plant that can resolve the food crisis—one that Lazy Pig’s family developed independently. That should go some way toward solving the citizens’ famine.”
“You’ve got a method for that?”
“Originally it was a problem I myself caused, so it would only make sense for Father to improve upon it and spread it, making it Father’s achievement.”
“If you make it too much about my own success, the Three Heroes Church starts paying attention, apparently. I mean… they really do come by for inspections a lot, don’t they. Every single time.”

Indeed. Every time we arrived at a town, they’d come poking through the inside of the tent under the pretense of an inspection. They’d dig around persistently, asking whether there were any human slaves inside. Of course there weren’t—every single one had been shipped off to Siltvelt. Because of this, apparently, the intake for those selling themselves into servitude had to be handled through a separate channel.
“It’s a bit sad that the slave trader’s reputation as third-rate is actually what turns a profit. The transactions in Siltvelt just keep piling up as a result.”

Well, well… things looked like they were going smoothly on the surface, but underneath, they really weren’t working out so well. The Bioplant truly needed to be unleashed, no question. And so it was decided—I would secure the Bioplant and spread it from Lazy Pig’s family home to every town and village, thereby loosening the grip on the citizens’ purse strings.
“Well, it’d be great if Motoyasu-kun’s idea lets us actually turn a profit within Melromarc.”
“Indeed it would.”

It was a shame I couldn’t make it Father’s achievement, but there was no helping it, I say. And so, chatting idly like this, Father and Older Sister sat drinking together while we waited for Panda to show up—except she never did. Elephant seemed to be searching for Panda too, going in and out of the tavern calling out to various acquaintances. Eventually, Elephant came back over to us.
“Elmelo-san, no sign of the person you’re after?”

“No. Since Spear Hero-sama wanted to have Lars meet Shield Hero-sama again for a talk, I asked around quite a bit. Apparently, right after that incident, she took on some job to clear her head and went off somewhere…”
“Oh dear.”
According to Elephant, apparently Panda had been displeased about being asked to guard Father on my behalf, and so she’d taken on some other, bigger job and left.
“Since she’s a mercenary, I suppose it’s possible, but what should we do? There’s no telling when she’ll be back… should we leave word and come see her again after some time passes?”
“Hmm. Motoyasu-kun, what kind of person is this, exactly?”
“Someone who gets along well with Father and Older Sister, and a talented individual capable of all sorts of things, I say.”
“Right, I heard that part, but…”
“I thought she’d be perfect for the circus, but the timing just didn’t align.”
“Perfect how?”
“To be specific, she is a panda beastwoman, I say.”
“Ahh…”
Father seemed to find that clicking into place, nodding several times.
“Yeah, that I can get behind. From a Japanese sensibility, that’s exactly the kind of spectacle-worthy slot we need.”
